boundary: The sealed confirmatory cohort was accessed by the transport, a question set was generated from it, and three pre-arm gates were measured on it. No arm ran, no answer was generated, no score exists, and no threshold, cohort, retriever, model or decoding parameter was changed as a result of any holdout observation.

defect.not_repaired_in_place: seal_w6_endpoint_v8.py is pinned by v8-post-open-instrumentation.json and the standing instruction is that it is not modified. Editing a sealing tool AFTER its outcome is known is exactly the class of change that must not be made quietly, so the omission is corrected here by binding rather than by editing. A filename-only repair is a founder decision, not mine.
defect.observation: seal_w6_endpoint_v8.py's ARM_RECEIPTS map was written before the gates ran and two of its filenames were guesses that turned out wrong: it expects v8-taint-gate-holdout.json (the file is v8-structural-taint-gate-holdout.json) and v8-baseline-validity-holdout.json (no such file exists --- the baseline validity gate IS the entity-conditioned gate, recorded as v8-entity-conditioned-gate-holdout.json).
defect.severity: the seal under-binds; nothing it states is false
defect.why_it_was_silent: when arms_ran is False the sealer treats a missing arm receipt as absent rather than as an error, and does not record that it expected one. So the seal bound 3 of 5 arm receipts and said nothing about the 2 it could not find. That is precisely the 'a gate silently omitted' hazard the sealer's own docstring names.

measured_cost.attribution_note: this is the whole day's pod billing on this account, which covers the deleted feasibility pod as well as ffsyr4qa8603rl. It is reported as measured provider billing, not as a per-arm inference cost --- no arm ran, so there is no inference cost to report.
